text: Vietnam's tea exports recover as shipments to Russia and US surge

Vietnam's tea exports showed signs of recovery in October 2026, with both volume and value increasing year-on-year, supported by higher average export prices and stronger demand from several key markets.

According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, Vietnam exported an estimated 15,600 tons of tea in October, worth $29.7 million, up 19.3% in volume and 30.4% in value compared with the same month last year.
The average export price reached $1,929 per ton, an increase of 9.3%.
In the first 10 months of 2026, tea exports totalled 105,300 tons, generating $197.4 million.
While export volume fell 4.6% year-on-year, export revenue rose 4.3%, with the average price climbing 9.3% to $1,874.3 per ton.
Pakistan remained Vietnam's largest tea export market, accounting for 20% of total shipments, followed by Taiwan (China) at 12.8% and China at 8.9%.
Meanwhile, Russia and the United States emerged as bright spots.
Shipments to Russia increased 32.4% in volume and 23.9% in value, while exports to the US rose 20.7% in volume and 43.4% in value, reflecting stronger demand from both markets.
